title: Main Sequence
body:
The **main sequence** is the stage where a star fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, and it
occupies about 90% of a star's life. That is why 90% of observed stars lie on the diagonal band
of the [[HR Diagram]].

Stability comes from a balance that corrects itself. Gravity pulls every layer inward, and the
pressure of the hot fusing core pushes outward, and the two match. If the core contracts
slightly it gets hotter, fusion speeds up, pressure rises, and it expands back. That thermostat
is why a star holds one luminosity for billions of years.

Fusion converts four hydrogen nuclei into one helium nucleus, and the helium weighs slightly
less than the four hydrogens did. The difference becomes energy through $E = mc^2$, and the Sun
converts about 4 million tonnes of mass into energy every second while losing a negligible
fraction of itself over its whole lifetime.

Mass decides everything else:

```
0.1 solar masses    dim, red, and stable for trillions of years
1   solar mass      the Sun, about 10 billion years
10  solar masses    thousands of times more luminous, and gone in a few million
```

A more massive star has more fuel and burns it disproportionately faster, so lifetime falls as
mass rises. That is why every very massive star observed is young, and why the massive stars
formed early in the universe are long gone.

The [[Solar Neutrino Problem]] is how the fusion model was tested, and the ending of
the main sequence is where the [[Red Giant]] stage begins.
